claim_one_line: R011 UPTAKE COMPLETES THE CODEX SET, AND IT FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN PAPER. (1) THE MISSING FENCE: the Sym-power identity was VERIFIED on Re(s) > 2+m, where every factor converges absolutely, and then EVALUATED AT s = 0 with no continuation step stated -- the licence is the identity theorem for meromorphic functions, and it must be said, because on the right the factors are no longer Euler products there. (2) A DUPLICATED LEAD-IN sentence left by my own earlier edit, appearing twice in the same subsection. Both fixed; paper rebuilds 7pp clean.
creates_law: AN IDENTITY IS FENCED BY WHERE IT WAS VERIFIED, NOT BY WHERE IT IS USED. eq:symfactor was checked as an identity of EULER PRODUCTS on Re(s) > 2+m and then used at s = 0, where the right-hand factors exist only by continuation. The step is standard -- both sides continue meromorphically, so the identity theorem gives agreement as meromorphic functions -- but omitting it lets a reader take the s = 0 display as verified when only its ancestor was. SCOPE: this is a fencing defect, not a false statement; the identity does hold at s = 0. SCOPE: it was found by auditing where each claim was VERIFIED against where it was USED, which is a check worth running on any paper that evaluates a product outside its half-plane of convergence.
